full_judgment: 15. Mr. Azizur Rahman Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the appellants, submits, that non-examination of material witnesses like member of union council, Abdus Sobban, Abdur Rahman and many elderly people of the locality who assembled in the place of occurrence, cast serious doubt in the prosecution case. P.W. 1 as well as P.W. 6 has admitted in their deposition that Abdus Sobhan and many people who assembled there to whom they had narrated the story and also named the names of the accused who actually assaulted and killed Farid but none of them were examined. Non-examination of these impartial witnesses, gives rise to a presumption adverse to the prosecution case. Had they been examined, possible they whould have disclosed the truth or at least they would have stated something which might not be favourable to the prosecution story. With holding of these materials witnesses has caused serious prejudice to the appellants. Next point that was urged before us is that non-production or non-seizing of the alamats like blood stained earth and shirt etc. cast a serious doubt as to the bonafide of the prosecution story. Mr. A. Rahman Chowdhury has placed before us the case of Abdul Bahar Vs. The state reported in B.L.D. 1985, wherein their Lordships held that non--production of alamats like blood stained earth and wearing apparels of the de-ceased, cast an adverse presumption against the prosecution story. In this case we have already observed that the prosecution failed to seize the blood-stained earth from the place of occurrence and also failed to seize the wearing apparels of Farid Miah. This has definitely cast an adverse presumption against the prosecution story rendering the same as unacceptable.
